title: Musicians' joy in their work; people judged by one skill
summary: Gil says musicians are lucky in their work though not in income. He criticises assuming that skill in one area means wisdom in all.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: One of the things that I have heard about musicians is that they love their work so much. And they work so hard because they do love it and I think as I look over the span of jobs that people have that perhaps musicians are the most
I think they are, musicians are very lucky.
Oh they are not lucky in as far as making a living.
No, but I'm talking about the sense of joy attached to their work because we know how many people are trapped into jobs that they just despise.

Along that line, it's a common mistake, oversight, lack of thought, lack of development whatever you want to call it amongst almost the whole world of adult population, not adult, all of it, they always judge a person by what they do. If they do a thing well they always seem to think that that person knows everything about all subjects well.
Because that person may know nothing about anything else in the world about what makes life work at all except what he does.

Not necessarily strictly musicians, but anybody who does anything. A man who builds bridges or whatever he does, a man is supposed to.... ........ There was a man in Sweden, what's his name, who writes sociological books on all this?

He once mentioned that of all these people that he had interviewed all over the world (what they considered the number one job?) or occupation, almost without exception they didn't know what they liked. Like anything else really. Like the old expression, their ass from a hole in the ground. They didn't know anything else really except that. They didn't know that.

Now, the problem with that is that people don't seem to be, to have been told or educated about that and they follow people that do one thing well and another thing that they do stupidly. That's the problem.
I just wanted to put that in When you're asking... (their ass from a hole in the ground?).
